  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Until further notice, meetings of the Inglewood Planning Commission will be
conducted pursuant to California Government Code section 54953(e), which
allows the City to use teleconferencing for members of the public to access
a meeting and to address the legislative body via a call-in option.

CALL-IN OPTION
1. Members of the public who wish to attend the Planning Commission Meeting
of December 7, 2022 and address the Planning Commission must use the call-
in option noted below:
Instructions: Dial one of the Phone Numbers below and when prompted,
enter the Access Code:
  Phone Number: 888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 6028910#
In the event of a disruption which prevents the City from broadcasting the
meeting to the public using the call-in option, or in the event of a
disruption within the City’s control which prevents the public from offering
public comments using the call-in option, the Planning Commission shall take
no further action on items appearing on the meeting agenda until public
access to the meeting via the call-in option is restored.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City also provides alternative methods for members of the public to
submit comments and/or to observe a public meeting. The following
alternative methods are provided to the public as a matter of convenience
only and the disruption in service to any alternative method does not
preclude the Planning Commission from taking further action on an agenda
item. In the event of a disruption to any alternative method below members
of the public should use the call-in option above.
2. Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may
choose to submit comments for consideration by the Planning Commission by
sending  them  to  Mindy  Wilcox,  AICP,  Planning  Manager  at
mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the
Planning Commission prior to consideration of the agenda, comments must be
received prior to 12:00 P.M. on the day of the meeting. Correspondence
should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after
12:00 P.M. and prior to the close of the public hearing will be made part
of the official public record of the meeting.
3. Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check
  with your cable provider for details
  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video at
  https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

Accessibility: If you will require special accommodations due to a
disability, please contact the Planning Division Office at (310) 412-5230,
One Manchester Boulevard, 4th Floor, Inglewood, California 90301.  All
requests for accommodations must be received 48 hours prior to the day of
the hearing.
Español: "Si no entiende esta noticia o si necesita más información, favor
de llamar a este número (310) 412-5230."

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 7, 2022

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, December 7, 2022, in the City
Council Chambers, on the ninth floor, of City Hall. Following the
Pledge of Allegiance by Commissioner Rice, the meeting was called
to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aidé Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams

Staff:  Christopher E. Jackson, ECD Director
  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner
  Art Salazar, Planner
  Christine Rivera, Assistant Planner
  Sean May, Planning Technician
  Michael Pan, Assistant City Attorney
  Cynthia Robinson, Secretary
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

Due to technical difficulties, there was a 10minute and 30
second postponement.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Ms. Mindy Wilcox stated -
1. Announced to the Commission the Annual Planning Commission
Holiday Luncheon on December 14th to be held at Hollywood Park
with a tour of the Intuit Dome and the Hollywood Park Retail area
under construction, and
2. Staff received correspondence from the applicant for item 7a to
postpone their item.
3. Item 7B, staff clarified that on the first page of the staff
report the number of conditions says three (3), but there are
actually four (4) conditions in the Resolution.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None (Confirmed by AT&T Operator).

(5) MINUTES APPROVAL:
Chairman Springs called for a motion to approve the November 2,
2022 minutes.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams made the Motion to Approve the November
2, 2022 Minutes and was seconded by Commissioner Patrick.

The motion passed with the following roll call vote:
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
December 7, 2022

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Shaw-Williams, and Chairman
  Springs.

Abstained:  Commissioners Rice and Trejo.

(6) PUBLIC HEARING:

6A. GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT NO. 2022-002 (GPA-2022-002).
A public hearing to consider General Plan Amendment 2022-002 (GPA-
2022-002) to update the Safety Element of the Inglewood General
Plan.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Trejo asked several questions of staff state approval
  of the Safety Element.
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

Chairman Springs asked several questions of staff.
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Chairman Springs’ questions.
   Mr. Jackson also responded to Chairman Springs' questions.

Chairman Springs invited the applicant to come forward to address
the Planning Commission regarding this item.

Consultants for the City – Raini Ott and Ethan Mobley, came before
the Planning Commission to thank them and the Planning Division
staff for all of their assistance and professionalism with regards
to ensuring the completion of the new General Plan Amendment so
that it can go before the City Council to be approved.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for the consultants.

Commissioner Rice asked the consultants several questions related
to the fire training facility in Inglewood.
   The Consultant responded to Commissioner Rice’s questions.

Commissioner Trejo asked the consultants several questions related
to a back-up emergency communications center.
   The Consultant responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the consultants a question
related to evacuation routes.
   The Consultant responded to Commissioner Shaw-Williams
  question.

Chairman Springs asked the AT&T Operator if there were any callers
on the line to speak for or against this item, there were none per
the AT&T Operator.

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and called for a motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Rice made the motion to affirm categorical exemption
EA-CE-2022-117 and adopt a resolution recommending City Council
adoption of GPA-2022-002 and was seconded by Commissioner Patrick
that Resolution No. 1943

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
December 7, 2022

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF
  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  RECOMMENDING CITY COUNCIL APPROVAL OF THE
  UPDATE TO THE SAFETY ELEMENT OF THE
  INGLEWOOD GENERAL PLAN.

Be approved.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams, and
  Chairman Springs.

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal process.

6B. ZONING CODE AMENDMENT NO. 2022-005 (ZCA-2022-005).
A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment 2022-005 (ZCA-
2022-005) to modify miscellaneous regulations in Chapter 12 of the
Inglewood Municipal Code related to Residential Accessory
Structures, Downtown Inglewood Development Standard Consistency,
Cosmetology Schools, Liquor Store State Code References, Signage
Regulation Consistency, and Floor Area Definition Citywide.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff a question related to outdoor dining.
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff a question related to beauty and
barber schools.
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams stated her support for facilitating the
operation of beauty/barber schools.

Chairman Springs asked staff questions related to Dwelling units,
  specifically ADUs and junior ADUs.
   Mr. McCrumby answered Chairman Springs’ questions.

Commissioner Rice made a concluding statement to staff in support
of facilitating the operation of beauty/barber schools.

Chairman Springs ask the AT&T Operator if there were any callers
on the line to speak for or against this item, there were none per
the AT&T Operator.

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and called for a motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Trejo made the motion to affirm categorical exemption
EA-CE-2022-114 and adopt a resolution recommending City Council
adoption of ZCA-2022-005 and was seconded by Commissioner Patrick
that Resolution No. 1944

December 7, 2022

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AND
  RECOMMENDING TO THE CITY COUNCIL FOR APPROVAL
  ZONING CODE AMENDMENT ZCA-2022-005 TO MODIFY

  COSMETOLOGY SCHOOLS, LIQUOR STORE STATE CODE
  REFERENCES, SIGNAGE REGULATION CONSISTENCY,

Be approved.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo Shaw-Williams, and

Ms. Wilcox explained there is no appeals process.

(7) NON-PUBLIC HEARING:

7A. DESIGN REVIEW 2022-012 (DR-2022-012).
A non-public hearing to consider Design Review 2022-012 (DR-2022-
012) to allow for a new, 5-story, 20-unit multi-family residential
building, on C-2(General Commercial)/MU-1A (Mixed-Use 1A Overlay)
zoned property at 3209 Imperial Highway.

This Item No.7A has been requested to be postponed by the
applicant.

7B. FINAL TRACT MAP NO. 80314-01 (FTM 80314-01).
A non-public hearing to consider Final Tract Map No. 80314-01
(FTM 80314-01) to finalize the subdivision of approximately
281.6 acres of the 298-acre Hollywood Park Specific Plan zoned
property at 1050 S. Prairie.

Ms. Wilcox stated that there is no staff presentation but staff is
available for any question the Commission may have.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff, there were none, and called for a motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Shaw-Williams made the motion to adopt the attached
resolution for FTM-80314-01 recommending approval of FTM-80314-01
to the Mayor and City Council subject to the 4 conditions and was
seconded by Commissioner Rice that Resolution No. 1945

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  RECOMMENDING APPROVAL TO THE CITY COUNCIL A
  FINAL TRACT MAP NO. 80314-01 FOR THE HOLLYWOOD
  PARK SPECIFIC PLAN ON AN APPROXIMATELY 281.6
  ACRE SITE AT 1050 SOUTH PRAIRIE AVENUE

Be approved.

  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
December 7, 2022

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams, and
  Chairman Springs.

Ms. Wilcox explained there is no appeals process.

(8)  PUBLIC COMMENTS:
1.  Applicant for Item 7B thanked Planning Staff for all of
  their hard work, due diligence, their assistance in working
  side by side with the applicant team in making sure that all
  protocols and directions for this item being approved this
  evening and it was a wonderful experience.

  Also thanked the Planning Commission for approving Item 7B
  and allowing the applicant firm to be of assistance to the
  City of Inglewood and looking forward to further future
  endeavors.

Chairman Springs closed the Public  Comments  asked  for  the
Planning Commission Initiatives.

(9) COMMISSION INITIATIVES:
Commissioner Patrick -
 Wanted to thank the Planning Staff for all of their hard work
  throughout the year by making sure that packets were made and
  delivered in plenty of time so that the Planning Commissioners
  had time enough to read them and that any questions the Planning
  Commission might have, Planning Staff would always have an
  answer.
 Expressed holiday best wishes.

Commissioner Rice –
 Also wanted to say thank you to the Planning Staff for everything
  they do all year long and how they listen to the Planning
  Commission as they evaluate what is good for the City of
  Inglewood.
 Expressed holiday best wishes and was pleased with the Tree
  Lighting Ceremony on the past Monday evening and the wonderful
  turn out from the community on the South lawn of City Hall.

Commissioner Trejo –
 Thank you also to the Planning Staff for always making sure that
  the Planning Commission is on top of what is happening here in
  the City of Inglewood as this small City is growing by leaps
  and bounds and how staff always listens to the Planning
  Commissioners to help them help Inglewood.
 Expressed holiday best wishes.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams –
 Agreed with all of the Planning Commissioners on how the
  Planning Staff do an amazing job in making sure the Planning
  Commissioners are able to a great job for the Inglewood
  Community.
 Expressed holiday best wishes.

 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
December 7, 2022

Chairman Springs –
 EV Charging Stations for the newest electrical vehicles that
  the Inglewood Community are now starting to utilize and are
  interested in owning.
   Mr. McCrumby answered Chairman Springs’ question.

  How much he enjoyed the Planning Commissioners training in
  Sacramento with the League of California Cities where both Mr.
  Jackson and Ms. Wilcox were instrumental in making that event
  possible for this year and is looking forward to 2023 training
  for the Planning Commissioners.
   Mr. Jackson answered Chairman Springs’ question.
   Ms. Wilcox answered Chairman Springs’ question.

  He stated that the city is growing by leaps and bounds and he
  remembers back to the late 60’s being here in Inglewood and
  how this City has completely changed over these past years,
  but know what is going on now in Inglewood is absolutely
  unprecedented. Inglewood is being looked at by all.
   Mr. Jackson answered Chairman Springs’ question.

  Expressed holiday best wishes.

The meeting was adjourned at 8:39pm.
